goal: Decide how a #loading boundary in the browser shows its fallback when data under it loads again, on the current runtime: Solid-style #loading (input) re-arm, a $fresh memo, or a hybrid

extra_axes.name: semantics
extra_axes.why: The candidates differ most in which reloads show the fallback (navigation-style input change vs any reload of a memo) and what readers outside the boundary see; device, time and tokens do not capture that.
extra_axes.ruling_why: the candidates differ mainly in which reloads show the fallback and what readers see; no other axis captures that

claims.text: Reads of a value that is still loading (no value yet) all have a defined path on main: a memo compute throws NotReady and the memo waits (startLoading); an effect skips its run and runs again when the value arrives; a handler or $client callback throws 'This value is still loading. Wait for it with await $resolve(memo), or check $isPending(memo) first' into the nearest #try; code that updates the page reads the promise. BRM182 is a compile error for such reads the compiler sees, unless guarded by $isPending or written as await $resolve(m). This corrects O6 of the superseded debate.
A memo that loads again keeps its old value and is pending; readers see the old value; $isPending is true. A plain read in a handler gives the last value during a reload (pending-handler-reads P3).

Solid 2 <Loading on>: `on` is a dependency list, a tracked function whose reads re-arm the boundary; its return value is never compared. A write to anything it reads makes the boundary fresh: if something under it is pending it shows the fallback until the new content is ready, else the notification is a no-op. Without `on`, a boundary that showed content keeps it through a refetch. Children stay alive behind the fallback. The same data read outside the boundary holds the frame so the fallback never shows (DEV LOADING_ON_OUTSIDE_HOLD). This corrects J10 of the superseded debate, which read `on` as naming the memos that load.

The browser has a pending boundary now: waits.ts on feat/browser-async (#413, settled-memo-merge) exports wait and fillSettled and has Boundary {n, done, f, w, c, o}, join/leave/fault/until/fillRange/bound/give. browser-loading-fallback (0.5.0 must, todo) will compile #loading in client mode to a boundary that shows #else while its body's memos with no value are pending, and keeps current content on an update. This corrects J2 of the superseded debate.
A #loading header is a compile error today (loading-header-error, 0.4.0): '#loading does not take a header yet'. The grammar parses #loading (expr) and LoadingBlock.on exists in the AST.

Settled elsewhere and binding here: the client-restructure debate (approved 2026-11-02) says pending and fallback state live in scope slots, no new hold-back helpers, and a browser render follows the server exactly; at equal size simpler wins. The superseded debate's user answers stand: $isPending is for styles, not #if inside the body (Q1); a fresh-only UI is wanted as an opt-in (Q3); no delay before the fallback (Q2).

Calibration: the superseded debate cost about 217k tokens over 2 rounds; M nodes on this roadmap cost 309k-834k (browser-await 834k); size budget per GOAL.md is todos within 0.3 kB per change, and the superseded estimate for option C was about 0.7 kB gzip in apps that use it, 0 otherwise.

Syntax and trigger (C): `#loading (expr) { ... } #else { ... }`. The header is a dependency list, as Solid 2's `on`: the compiler makes it an update of the boundary on the slots it reads, its value is never compared, and a write to any of those slots re-arms the boundary. Without a header, behavior is exactly browser-loading-fallback's (keep content on an update), so a refresh() or a write the header does not read keeps stale content plus $isPending.

evidence.detail: Solid 2 re-arms per boundary from what `on` reads (J3); React resets a boundary to its fallback on navigation by keying it on the route, i.e. the trigger is a named input, not the data. Both keep refetches stale by default, matching J6 Q3 (fresh-only UI as an opt-in).

claims.ruling_why: superseded by P9: the header names memos (J9)

claims.text: Which reads count: after the pass of the re-arming write drains, the boundary shows #else if anything under it is pending: the slots of its own scope that the body reads (a list the compiler emits) and any loadingSlots key whose scope's p/o chain reaches the body scope. It releases when none is pending, checked with waits.ts `until`. Memos read only outside the body never count; nothing pending at re-arm is a no-op, as in Solid.

evidence.source: packages/brumate/src/runtime/client/updates.ts:254-259 (startLoading runs in the pass), :544-549 (pending); runtime/client/state.ts:261 (loadingSlots keyed scope:slot); runtime/client/branches.ts:255 (hidden() walks p/o, the same walk); evidence/client-pending-boundary.md (until)
evidence.detail: Memos start loading synchronously inside the write's drain, so a check queued after the drain sees every reload the write caused, with no new subscription.

claims.ruling_why: O3: counting every loading slot under the body includes $debounced/$throttled timers and memos only effects or handlers read; the check must be the reads that render the body

claims.text: Mechanism, built on browser-loading-fallback's boundary: on arm, move the body's nodes into a fragment held like a Boundary with c = the write count, and insert #else; on release, put the same nodes back and let give() run the updates the held body missed when the count differs. Children stay alive (same DOM nodes, input values, scopes, no re-render), and no `hiding` is needed, which would add about 1.1 kB gzip to apps without #offscreen.

evidence.source: evidence/client-pending-boundary.md (give runs all updates of a held body's scopes when c differs; blocks find their markers in the page); esbuild --minify | gzip -9 on branches.ts offscreen+hiding

claims.ruling_why: O1 and O2: a detached body keeps portals, window/document listeners and effects running against the #offscreen rules, and misses updates that would open branches, so the fallback releases early

claims.text: Readers outside the boundary do not change: handlers, $client callbacks, effects and markup outside the body read the old value with $isPending true (J2), so there is no new throw path and BRM182 is untouched. Effects inside the held body keep running (alive behind the fallback, as Solid). There is no frame hold, so a read outside shows stale data while the boundary shows #else; the docs say so instead of Solid's DEV LOADING_ON_OUTSIDE_HOLD warning.

evidence.detail: J1 paths stay reserved for first loads; the reload path of J2 stays the only reload path.

claims.ruling_why: Q2: the body kept behind the fallback follows the #offscreen rules, so readers and effects inside it pause

claims.text: Server and resume: the server renders a header #loading as a headerless one and never evaluates the header (it compiles into client code only), so first loads stream fallback then body as today. Only header blocks write markers around the body range and ship their #else template, behind a new features.ts flag. A re-arm while the streamed body has not arrived is a no-op since the fallback is still up, which replaces the old debate's first-settle bit.

claims.text: (A) `$fresh` memo: a reload writes the in-flight promise into the slot so J1 paths handle readers. Runtime is small (about 0.1 kB, a branch in asyncMemo) but: every handler read of a $fresh memo becomes BRM182 unless guarded, even one markup reads outside #loading; markup outside any boundary goes empty during a reload (memo-prop-browser-child); browser-loading-fallback keeps content on an update, so it still needs a new path for a slot that turns back into a promise; and the choice is per memo, so it cannot tell a navigation from a refresh() or differ between two boundaries reading one memo.

evidence.detail: React's default (an update that suspends shows the fallback again) was found too aggressive and transitions were added to opt out; A re-creates that default per memo. Svelte 5 boundaries show pending only on the first render and use $effect.pending() after.

claims.text: (H) Header re-arm as in P1, but the boundary re-renders its body from scratch through `bound`, as `#key` would, so pending reads are first loads under J1 and browser-loading-fallback's path. About 0.2 kB, but it drops DOM nodes, input state and child scripts on every re-arm and re-runs child memos, against the superseded debate's accepted test (same DOM nodes and input state) and Solid's alive-behind-fallback.

evidence.detail: React's key reset loses state, which is why it is documented for navigations only.

claims.text: Detaching the body is not 'no hiding needed': it skips three things hiding does on main. A #portal in the body (a dialog) stays on screen elsewhere in the page, <window>/<document> listeners in the body keep firing, and effects keep running against nodes that are out of the page, against the #offscreen rule in decisions.md:96-98. A moved iframe reloads and focus is lost. Likely in any body with a dialog, a key listener or an effect that measures DOM; matching #offscreen brings back most of hiding's code. (Filed on time, as rework of the node, since semantics is not ruled yet; it belongs on semantics if that axis is accepted.)

With the body out of the page, no update reaches it during the hold (blockStart, text and findComment need connected markers). So an #if or #for row that a settled memo would open does not render, and its loads do not start. The pending check then sees nothing, releases the fallback, and give() opens the branch after the fallback is gone, showing empty text or a nested fallback. The content the header was meant to hold escapes as a second loading phase. Certain whenever the body branches on reloaded data. (Filed on time, as rework of the node, since semantics is not ruled yet; it belongs on semantics if that axis is accepted.)

claims.text: P2 counts every loadingSlots key under the body, not the reads that render it. $debounced and $throttled memos are in loadingSlots while their timer waits, with no load in flight. Memos that only an effect, a handler or a $isPending style reads count too. So the fallback can show, or stay up, for a debounce delay or a child's background reload that the body never waits on. Solid counts only pending reads under the boundary. (Filed on time, as rework of the node, since semantics is not ruled yet; it belongs on semantics if that axis is accepted.)

The size case for detaching overstates hiding. Without offscreen() (280 B), hiding is 955 B gzip by the same proxy, not 1129 B, and 0 B extra in apps that already ship #offscreen. P6's 0.4 kB is reasoning, not a measurement. Fixing O1 adds portal, listener and effect handling on top, so the gap between detach and hiding is under 0.5 kB, and only in apps that have a header block and no #offscreen.

Keep the superseded debate's step-2 mechanism and call hiding.hide(bodyScope, start, end) directly on a re-arm, keeping the body in the page. This keeps P1's trigger and P2's check. Updates land while the body is hidden, so the O2 branches open and their loads join the hold, with no give() rerun and no index misses. Portals, listeners and effects follow the #offscreen rule. Cost is at most 955 B gzip in header apps without #offscreen (O4). The old risk O10 does not apply, since the boundary passes the body scope and markers directly instead of searching scope.children.

claims.text: Navigation never reaches a re-arm or a $fresh memo in brumate. A client navigation keeps a layout with the same key and replaces every other route with the server's markup, which streams fallback then body. So React's key-on-route prior art does not carry over, and P7's 'cannot tell a navigation from refresh()' reduces to 'cannot tell an in-page input write from refresh()'. That still holds against $fresh, but the header's use is in-page state (a selected id, a query), which Q1 should be read against.

P5 underscopes the markers. A headerless #loading whose body cannot wait has no boundary and no markers (markup.ts:2179-2185). The streaming marker <!--l<boundary>--> carries no scope id or anchor, so the client cannot find it from its scope. A header block needs a new marker form in both server branches, and rangeEnd must count it. That is the superseded debate's O9 (upheld), which P5 does not carry forward.

During a detach hold, every update aimed at the body misses. findComment re-reads observer records, findElement falls back to document.querySelector of the whole page per bound element, and sweepIndexes may drop the body's index entries. Then give() runs all the body's updates again. For a list body of N bound rows, that is N full-document queries plus a second pass; hiding avoids both because the nodes stay connected.

Solid documents `on` as telling an identity change from a refetch: 'Depend on the route: a navigation shows the skeleton with the new route while the page loads; a refetch of the same route keeps the page visible', and `on={[query(), page()]}` for results. In brumate, which holds no frame, an input write updates everything outside the boundary at once while the memo under it keeps the old value (J2), so the page shows the new input next to the old record's body.

The trigger the maintainer wants is a memo update: a way for the author to make a memo that loads again show the boundary's fallback (Q1). Telling an input write from a refresh() is not the point; Solid's input-based `on` (J3, J8) is prior art for the hold, not the required trigger.
P1 amended: the header names memos, not inputs. `#loading (user)` re-arms on an update of `user` (it goes pending), whatever caused it, instead of on a write to what the header reads.
claims.why: J9 (Q1): the wanted trigger is a memo update the author opts into; O3: only reads that render the body may count

claims.text: (C') Syntax and trigger: `#loading (user, posts) { ... } #else { ... }`. Each name must be a memo (including $debounced/$throttled) of the component or of a block script around the block, and markup in the body must read it, else a compile error; so only reads that render the body count (O3). While the boundary shows content, a named memo that goes pending for any cause (an input write, refresh(), a new stream) shows #else; unnamed memos in the body keep stale content plus $isPending. The header compiles to an update on the named slots, as `$isPending(user)` in an attribute does, since startLoading already triggers readers when a memo starts loading.

claims.text: P11's 'a branch that opens under the hidden body joins the Boundary' is not what waits.ts does. join() counts only in the render that is running (module `boundary`, set by within() for bound and fillRange). An #if that an update opens during the drain runs outside it, so its waits fill in place, and a plain $memo there is not a wait at all. The body therefore shows with that branch still loading, which is O2 again. A fix needs updates under a header body to run within the header boundary, plus a count for memos with no value: a change to the frozen contract v1, whose re-review removed exactly that walk of held scopes.

claims.text: P10 can name only memos of the component or of a block script around the block. A memo that a child component in the body loads for itself (`<UserCard id={id}/>`), and a chained memo (posts = $memo(getPosts(user.id))) that is not named, release with the named memo and show stale or empty content after #else. The author must lift each such memo into the parent and name it. That is a limit Solid's `on` does not have, since it holds for every pending read under the boundary.

claims.text: Hiding sets display:none !important on the body's top-level elements, and a hidden element loses focus. A named memo whose input field sits inside the body, which is common for search, hides the field on the first keystroke. A named $debounced memo, which P10 allows, hides the body for the whole wait even when nothing loads. This is likely in search UIs; it needs a compile warning, or docs that say to keep the control outside the body.

claims.text: Final structure: `#loading (m, ...) { ... } #else { ... }` names memos of the component or of a block script around the block that the body renders from (P10). It hides the body with hiding under the #offscreen rules (P12, Q2) while any named memo is pending, with no nested join (P17), and the server renders it as a headerless block (P5, O7 markers). For O10, the compiler adds to the header's list the memos of the same scope that the body renders and that read a named memo (posts of user), which it already tracks for `$isPending`, so a chain releases together; a memo a child loads for itself is a stated limit, and the child takes its own `#loading (m)`. For O11, the docs say to keep the control that writes a named memo's input outside the body, and a compile warning flags a named memo that is, or reads, a $debounced or $throttled memo, since it hides the body for the whole wait. `#key` rebuild stays a docs idiom (P13); $fresh is not adopted (P15).

claims.text: P18's chain rule runs the list the wrong way. The $isPending list is upstream: $isPending(m) reads m and upstreamMemos(m), the memos that m itself reads (model.ts:234-252, rewrite.ts:461). For a named user, that does not give posts, which reads user. Adding the downstream readers needs a new inverted walk over the model's sites. Cheaper and exact: the header pending-checks [m, ...upstreamMemos(m)] for each name, the same set $isPending uses, and the docs say to name the memo the body renders from last (#loading (posts) also holds while user loads). The $debounced warning reuses the same upstream list.

questions.ask: In a #loading block that opts into showing its fallback again, should a reload that an action's refresh() causes (same inputs, newer data) also show the fallback, or only a change of the inputs the header names (such as the route or an id)?
questions.answer: Neither option fits the goal of the node: brumate has no way to make a memo update show the loading boundary's fallback. The feature is that way (the maintainer, 2026-11-02).

questions.ask: While a #loading block shows its fallback again over content that stays alive, should that hidden content follow the #offscreen rules (effects pause, <window>/<document> listeners stop, dialogs opened through #portal hide), or should its effects and listeners keep running as if it were visible?
questions.answer: The #offscreen rules: effects pause, window/document listeners stop, portals hide.

questions.ask: When the header's input names a different record (a new id), should the debate weigh rebuilding the body, such as #key (id) { #loading {...} #else {...} } with no new syntax, against keeping it alive?
